claim: The 0.56-lunar-mass value is the reported 100-day J1744-1134 minimum detectable mass.
The published limit uses circular orbits and a 90 percent injection-recovery boundary.
limitations: The paper calls the table confidence level although the method is recovery completeness

claim: The published table values include a generic factor 2.5 timing-fit sensitivity penalty calibrated on one synthetic pulsar.
The published injections use Gaussian white noise at the TOA uncertainties and omit the release white-noise model from the analyzed residuals.
Pilot 1 and the published value are not method-identical estimates of the same experiment.
limitations: Method non-equivalence does not identify which pipeline gives the better real-world limit

claim: The Pilot 1 timing-amplitude to projected-mass conversion is correct for the low-companion-mass circular projected orbit convention.
evidence_type: independent calculation and exact two-body solution
limitations: Assumes projected circular orbit and stated central mass

claim: Changing the assumed central mass from 1.4 to 1.5 solar masses changes the implied timing amplitude by only 4.50 percent.
The released-covariance model passes the predeclared hard non-periodic residual diagnostics for J1744.
limitations: Excess kurtosis is an advisory failure and nonstationary structure is not excluded
